INFINITY GRID — SCOUT2-B V1.6 FIXED-POINT EXTERNAL INTERFACE THEOREM
27 AUGUST 2026

SCOPE
This theorem concerns only the externally visible port/interface behavior generated by the two currently earned O2 operations:
  RANK-LIFT and RELATION-ADD.
It does not quotient away intrinsic typed-incidence topology from the exact relational carrier, and it introduces no geometry, time, actualization, deletion, rewiring, probability, direction, or physics.

DATA
Let A be the frozen seven-port alphabet. For every mature node v let
  p_v in N^7
be its exact port-counter vector. For a connected exact carrier G, let E be its retained typed-incidence multiset and define
  u_v(a) = number of retained edge endpoints incident on node v through port type a.
Capacity validity is u_v <= p_v coordinatewise. Define free capacity f_v=p_v-u_v.

Define the anonymous distributed capacity-reservation interface

  Q(G) = multiset_v (p_v,u_v) / anonymous-node permutation.

Equivalently Q may be encoded as (p_v,f_v) or (u_v,f_v), because p=u+f.
Q deliberately omits T and exact endpoint pairing/topology.

THEOREM
For the currently earned operation algebra {RANK-LIFT, RELATION-ADD}, Q is a transition-congruent, closed external interface. Thus if exact carriers G and H have Q(G)=Q(H), then every finite action-labelled future tree of Q-states reachable from G is identical to that reachable from H.

PROOF
1. RELATION-ADD.
A legal addition chooses two distinct nodes v,w and compatible endpoint types a,b. Its legality is exactly
  p_v(a)-u_v(a) > 0,
  p_w(b)-u_w(b) > 0,
  Bridge(a,b)=true.
These quantities are all determined by Q and the frozen Bridge table. The successor leaves p unchanged and increments u_v(a) and u_w(b) by one. Because Q retains the multiset of local (p,u) colors and their multiplicities, the anonymous successor Q is determined by Q plus the chosen action. Exact pre-existing endpoint pairing is never read by the frozen relation-add rule.

2. RANK-LIFT.
Each of the 77 frozen mature-node templates supplies a fixed source-port index s and fixed port delta dp (with every coordinate >= -1). For a local state (p,u), the strict/cross eligibility tests read only p,u and the fixed template. If legal, the successor changes p to p+dp at one node and leaves u unchanged. T may change in the exact carrier but is not read for eligibility and is omitted from Q. Hence the labelled successor Q is determined by Q and the template/mode.

3. CLOSURE.
Both operations map Q-states to Q-states of the same schema.

4. FINITE-DEPTH INDUCTION.
At depth 0, Q-equivalent carriers have the same Q. Assume their action-labelled Q-future trees agree through depth n. By 1-3 they have exactly the same labelled Q-successors, and each corresponding successor is again Q-equivalent; applying the induction hypothesis gives identical trees through depth n+1. Therefore equality holds for every finite depth.

5. T.
The frozen Bridge and RANK-LIFT eligibility/capacity conditions never read T. T remains necessary for exact algebraic identity, but not for Q-dynamics.

LIMITS
- This is an external-behavior quotient, not a claim that graph topology is intrinsically nonexistent or irrelevant.
- Any future earned operation that explicitly reads path, cycle, endpoint pairing, topology, T, ancestry, geometry, deletion/rewiring, etc. reopens the theorem.
- Q is proved sufficient here; minimality is NOT proved.
- Duplicate microscopic/exact witnesses are deduplicated as set-valued possibilities, matching the existing O1 behavioral-relation convention.

SCOUT3 R3 FUTURE-CONTROL QUOTIENT THEOREM
Date: 2026-08-27
Status: EARNED WITHIN THE FROZEN SCOUT3 OPERATION SET; NOT O3 GRADUATION

DEFINITION
For an exact Scout3 O3 carrier H, let each constituent O2 entity v contain anonymous O1 interface sites i.
Each site has exact mature-node capacity vector p_vi in N^7, inherited O2 reservation vector u2_vi in N^7, and O3 reservation vector U3_vi in N^7 induced by retained inter-O2 relations.
Define exact free capacity

    f_vi = p_vi - u2_vi - U3_vi.

Define

    R3(H) = multiset_v [ multiset_i (p_vi, f_vi) ].

Both the entity blocks and the sites inside each block are anonymous. The block boundary is retained: sites belonging to the same O2 entity remain grouped together.

THEOREM
For the frozen Scout3 operation set:

  1. O3 RELATION-ADD,
  2. embedded O2 RANK-LIFT,
  3. embedded internal-O2 RELATION-ADD,
  4. FRESH-O2-ENTITY insertion followed by one O3 relation,

R3 is an exact future-control quotient. If R3(H)=R3(H'), then the complete legal action-labelled successor R3 sets of H and H' are identical for each of these operation families. By induction, every finite future built only from these operations has the same R3-labelled possibility tree.

PROOF
1. O3 RELATION-ADD.
A legal action chooses two distinct O2 entity blocks, one site in each block, and port types a,b. Legality is exactly:

    f_vi[a] > 0,
    f_wj[b] > 0,
    Bridge(a,b).

Bridge is frozen. The successor changes only

    f_vi[a] -> f_vi[a]-1,
    f_wj[b] -> f_wj[b]-1.

Therefore legality and successor R3 depend only on R3.

2. Embedded O2 RANK-LIFT.
A frozen template t supplies a source type s and delta vector dp. In the audited code the action requires p[s]>0, p+dp>=0, and either:

    strict: f[s] > 0,

or the cross-capacity condition

    p+dp >= total_reservation.

But total_reservation = u2+U3 = p-f, so the cross condition is exactly

    f+dp >= 0.

The successor is

    p' = p+dp,
    f' = f+dp.

Thus both legality and output depend only on (p,f), hence only on R3.

3. Embedded internal-O2 RELATION-ADD.
A legal internal action chooses two distinct sites inside the same retained O2 entity block and compatible port types with positive free capacities. It decrements the corresponding two entries of f by one. No exact internal edge pairing is read. The entity block boundary is sufficient and necessary for distinguishing same-entity from different-entity actions.

4. FRESH-O2-ENTITY growth.
A fresh graduated Q entity supplies exact site states (p,u2). Before any O3 attachment its O3 reservation is zero, so its R3 site state is (p,p-u2). Appending that block and making one O3 relation is therefore completely determined by the old R3, the supplied fresh Q block, and the relation-add rule from part 1.

5. Finite future.
Each operation maps an R3 class to an R3 class without consulting hidden information. Structural induction on any finite operation sequence gives equality of the complete action-labelled R3 possibility trees.

WHAT R3 HIDES
The theorem shows that, for these frozen operations, future control does not require:

- exact O3 edge pairing/topology,
- which reservations were made internally at O2 versus externally at O3,
- entity names,
- exact construction history/parentage.

WHAT R3 MUST RETAIN
- Exact p cannot in general be discarded: actual source-bank sites with the same free vector f admit different RANK-LIFT template sets when p differs.
- O2 entity block grouping cannot be discarded: actual exact carriers with the same flattened site-state multiset but different block grouping have different relation-add and internal-relation successor sets.

EMPIRICAL ADVERSARIAL SUPPORT
Across the selected r0-r64 panels, 85 R3 classes contain multiple distinct exact carriers; 12 of these also hide different splits between u2 and U3.
A concrete r3=3 pair with identical R3 but different (u2,U3) provenance has identical complete successor R3 sets under:
- 8/8 O3 relation-add successor classes,
- 83/83 rank-lift successor classes,
- 2/2 internal-relation successor classes,
- all 1,039 legal fresh-growth actions against the frozen 16-source audit panel, collapsing to identical 976 R3 successor classes.
These computations support the theorem but are not the source of its generality; the generality follows from the read/write proof above.

SCOPE / REOPEN RULE
R3 is a future-control quotient only for the frozen Scout3 operations listed above. It deliberately does not preserve exact topology-derived Scout observer labels such as articulation, cycle arrangement or parallel-edge arrangement. If a future O3/O4 operation reads exact O3 topology, reservation provenance, ancestry, or any other hidden field, R3 must be reopened and re-audited.

NON-CLAIM
This theorem does not graduate O3. It does not yet establish O3-as-entity macro composition/substitution closure, an O3 phase boundary, a unique/minimal interface, or prospective higher-tier persistence.

# Formal Foundation v2.2 - Audit and Closeout

**Verdict:** PASS WITH PRECISION CORRECTIONS. No numerical or witness result collapsed. The interrupted pass was scientifically salvageable and is now closed as an audited v2.2 edition.

## Corrections made

1. **Bounded depth and all-finite future were separated.** For a finite depth `d`, `P_d` is the coarsest exact depth-`d` observational quotient; it need not be a reusable transition congruence. The stabilized `P_*` is the all-finite-future reusable quotient. This is the most important conceptual repair because IN11's 2,864-class current-enabledness quotient is intentionally bounded and not transition-congruent.
2. **Set and multiplicity semantics were separated.** Under set-valued successors, `P_*` is ordinary observer-respecting strong bisimulation. Under `Counter` semantics, it is an exact multiplicity-stable transition congruence, not ordinary strong bisimulation.
3. **External bibliography metadata was repaired.** The Park venue was made precise and the Ranzato-Tapparo DOI was added.
4. **The mature observer-resolution census was replayed deterministically.** Its class counts and authoritative lattice result reproduced exactly.

## Results surviving audit

- 7 mature port atoms -> 5 bridge-only atom classes; automorphism group size 4.
- Supplied mature panel: 22,885 exact states, 7,600 port states, 5,241 bridge-multiplicity classes, 64 support/rank-enabled classes, 4 bridge-acceptance classes.
- Bridge multiplicity has the exact five-counter aggregate `(p0+p1,p2,p3,p4,p5+p6)`; a 5x5 response minor is unimodular.
- Template-labelled port children reconstruct parent `p`; template-labelled exact children reconstruct `(p,t)` in the frozen isolated 77-template grammar.
- IN11 current enabledness: A4 3,240 -> exact bounded observer quotient 2,864; A4 sufficient, not minimal.
- O2 Q: actual generated k17 witness proves sitewise `(p,f)` pairing necessary.
- O3 R3: constructive connected witness proves sitewise `(p,f)` pairing inside blocks necessary; rank and internal-relation futures separate the pair.
- Q and R3 remain future-sufficient for their frozen operation algebras; global minimality remains open.

## Replay status

A fresh clean replay reproduced byte-identically the generic theorem-shape tests, mature information lattice and witnesses, mature observer-resolution census, O2 pairing witness and O3 pairing witness. The IN11 computation is substantially heavier; its two archived executions in the salvage checkpoint are byte-identical for both result and witness. A third foreground replay was attempted during this closeout but exceeded the current execution window before completion; no scientific claim depends on that third run.

## Open boundary

The next phase is guarded nonnegative mature reachability, unless global Q/R3 minimality is deliberately prioritized first.

## Certified replay-runner closeout

The final packaging audit found one reproducibility-controller defect: Stage 8 invoked
an alternate aggregate-schema builder rather than the authoritative frozen assembler.
The underlying nine component results/witnesses all reproduced exactly. The controller
was repaired to call `assemble_observer_hierarchy.py`, and resumable fail-closed
checkpointing was added.

A clean staged replay from the included source archives then regenerated all ten frozen
machine-readable outputs under `PYTHONHASHSEED=999`: **10/10 byte-identical, 0
mismatches**. The repair changed no scientific result or claim.

# Part I - The question made precise

## 1. Sufficiency is not minimality

The closed finite algebra was designed to support exact substitution. If a microscopic composite `X` is replaced by its complete boundary relation `T_X`, every later legal composition produces the same full relation and the same tied-max selection, modulo anonymous-interface isomorphism. This is a soundness or sufficiency theorem:

$$q(x)=q(y) \Longrightarrow x\equiv_{\mathrm{ctx}}y.$$

Here `q` is the canonical boundary map and contextual equivalence means that no admitted finite context distinguishes the two objects.

This implication is the one needed for safe black-box replacement. It says the boundary never hides information that the frozen compositor can later require.

Minimality asks for the converse:

$$x\equiv_{\mathrm{ctx}}y \Longrightarrow q(x)=q(y).$$

If both directions hold, the boundary is fully abstract relative to the chosen observation and context language. But the phrase “chosen observation” cannot be omitted. A context that is allowed to read the complete exact boundary distinguishes every different exact record immediately. A context that asks only “Can this endpoint connect?” can collapse distinctions that exact successor identity needs.

### Plain-language version

A passport contains more information than a ticket inspector needs. It may still be the right exact document for international travel. Asking whether the passport is “minimal” makes no sense until we say which official is looking and what decision that official must make.

The same is true here. IG has one exact state language and several smaller exact control languages.

## 2. The observer contract

We freeze an observer contract

$$\mathfrak O=(S,A,\to,O,M,D).$$

Its components are:

- `S`: the state population being classified;
- `A`: the admitted action or context labels;
- `→`: the action-labelled transition relation;
- `O`: the terminal observation returned at the current state;
- `M`: set-valued or multiplicity-sensitive successor semantics;
- `D`: a fixed finite depth or all finite depths.

Every one of these choices matters.

### 2.1 Population

A quotient may be minimal on a supplied finite panel and fail when a new state is added. The 22,885 mature-state result is therefore panel-relative. O2 Q and O3 R3, by contrast, have symbolic future-control proofs for their frozen operations, but their global minimality has not been proved.

### 2.2 Actions and contexts

Q hides exact O2 topology because the frozen O2 operations do not read it. R3 hides exact O3 topology and reservation provenance because the frozen O3 resource operations do not read them. Adding an operation that asks for articulation structure or a specific endpoint pairing reopens the quotient.

### 2.3 Terminal observation

An exact-boundary observer sees all canonical state immediately. A bridge observer sees only compatibility. A current-enabledness observer sees which actions are legal now. A successor observer additionally sees where those actions lead.

### 2.4 Multiplicity semantics

Two states can have the same set of possible successor classes while having different numbers of microscopic ways to reach them. If multiplicity is operationally visible, a `Counter` profile is required. If only possibility is visible, set semantics is the correct quotient. v2.2 makes this choice explicit rather than allowing it to drift between audits.

### 2.5 Depth

Current enabledness is depth zero or one, depending on convention. One-step successor equality is stronger. Equality of all finite observation trees is stronger again. A quotient that is exact at depth one can fail at depth two.

> **Freeze rule.** Any change to `S`, `A`, `O`, `M`, or `D` reopens the minimality claim.

### 2.6 Bounded observational minimality versus reusable congruence

The depth coordinate `D` creates two mathematically different targets. If `D=d<\infty`, the exact minimal classifier for the declared observation trees through depth `d` is `P_d`. It may merge states whose successors differ in ways that become visible only after depth `d`, so it is not automatically a transition congruence for continued reuse. If `D` means **all finite depths**, refinement is continued to the stable partition `P_*`; that fixed point is the reusable future-control quotient. This distinction is essential for interpreting IN11: its 2,864-class current-enabledness quotient is an exact bounded observer quotient, not an all-future dynamic state.

# Part II - The finite full-abstraction theorem

## 3. Observer refinement

Let `P_0` be the partition induced by current observation:

$$s\equiv_0 t \iff O(s)=O(t).$$

Suppose `P_n` is known. Replace each successor state by its `P_n` block. For every action `a`, record the resulting successor-block profile. Under possibility semantics this profile is a set. Under multiplicity semantics it is a multiset or `Counter`.

Define

$$s\equiv_{n+1}t$$

iff:

1. `O(s)=O(t)`, and
2. for every action `a`, the `a`-successor profiles of `s` and `t` agree after quotienting by `P_n`.

This is ordinary partition refinement expressed in the language needed by the IG hierarchy.

## 4. Finite stabilization theorem

**Theorem FF22-T1 - Finite observer refinement.** Let `S` and `A` be finite. The sequence

$$P_0 \succeq P_1 \succeq P_2 \succeq \cdots$$

stabilizes after at most

$$|S|-|P_0|$$

strict refinement rounds.

**Reason.** Every strict refinement increases the number of blocks by at least one. No partition of `S` has more than `|S|` blocks.

## 5. Coarsest congruence theorem

**Theorem FF22-T2 - Coarsest observer-respecting stable equivalence.** The stable partition `P_*` is the unique coarsest equivalence relation that:

- respects the terminal observation, and
- is stable under every admitted action with the declared successor-profile semantics.

Under ordinary set-valued successor semantics this is the coarsest observer-respecting strong bisimulation on the frozen finite labelled transition system. Under `Counter` semantics it is instead the coarsest exact **multiplicity-stable transition congruence**: successor multiplicities into quotient blocks must agree. Calling the latter ordinary strong bisimulation would be imprecise.

Any other equivalence stable under the same declared semantics refines `P_*`. The proof is the standard fixed-point/coinductive argument. At a fixed point, equivalent states have equal observations and equal successor profiles into fixed-point blocks. Conversely, any stable equivalence cannot merge states that the iterative signatures split.

## 6. Full abstraction for finite observation trees

**Theorem FF22-T3a - Bounded-depth observational minimality.** For each finite depth `d`, two states lie in the same block of `P_d` iff their action-labelled observation trees agree through depth `d`. Consequently `P_d` is the coarsest exact quotient for that bounded observer question. No transition-congruence claim beyond depth `d` follows merely from this statement.

**Theorem FF22-T3b - All-finite-depth full abstraction.** Two states lie in the same stable block `P_*` iff they generate the same action-labelled observation tree at every finite depth under the frozen observer contract.

For the all-finite-depth contract this gives both soundness and completeness:

$$s\equiv_* t \iff \mathrm{Tree}_n(s)=\mathrm{Tree}_n(t)\quad\text{for every finite }n.$$

Every strict refinement supplies a finite-depth separator. If two states first split from `P_n` to `P_{n+1}`, some action leads to successor profiles already distinguishable at depth `n`; appending that action yields a depth-`n+1` separating experiment.

### 6.1 What this theorem does not do automatically

It does not turn a variable-size infinite generated family into a finite state system. Applying the algorithm to O2 or O3 globally requires either:

- a finite transition-closed population;
- a finite symbolic presentation whose refinement is itself decidable; or
- an independent structural proof that a proposed quotient is coarsest.

The existing Q and R3 theorems provide sufficiency for all finite frozen futures. They do not yet provide global minimality.

## 7. Executable theorem-shape tests

The clean-room reference implementation includes five exact tests:

1. a pair separated only by a depth-two experiment;
2. a pair merged under set semantics but separated when multiplicity is observed;
3. agreement between iterative refinement and bounded observation trees;
4. agreement with a brute-force tiny coarsest stable partition;
5. the finite stabilization bound.

All **5/5** tests pass. These tests validate the implementation shape; the general theorem is mathematical and does not depend on the finite test count.

# Part VIII - Falsifications and corrections

## 29. “The boundary is minimal” is retracted as an unqualified sentence

The finite core proves a sufficient exact boundary. It does not prove that the same boundary is minimal for every reduced observer. v2.2 therefore bars the sentence “the IG boundary is minimal” unless the observer contract is stated immediately.

## 30. A4 minimality is falsified

A4 remains a valuable exact abstraction for current move support, but its 3,240 classes retain 376 distinctions invisible to the frozen d78-d109 current-enabledness observer. The correct status is “sufficient but not minimal.”

## 31. Independent p-bags and f-bags are falsified

At O2 and O3, it is not enough to know which capacity vectors exist and which free-capacity vectors exist. The pairing tells us which template opportunities and reservations coexist at one site. The new witnesses make this necessity concrete.

## 32. R3 as complete topology is falsified

R3 intentionally hides exact topology. Same-R3 carriers can have different articulation and parallel-edge structure. This is not a defect in the R3 theorem because the frozen resource operations do not read those properties. It becomes a defect only if one silently changes the observer.

## 33. Fixed-size atomicity remains unearned

Neither O2 nor O3 has a fixed-size exact local state independent of the number of constituent sites or blocks. Graduation does not change that. “Atomic O2 node” and “atomic O3 node” remain unauthorized without a new theorem.

# 1. Observer contracts

Let

$$\mathfrak O=(S,A,\to,O,M,D)$$

be an observer contract, where:

- `S` is a finite set of states;
- `A` is a finite action alphabet;
- `s -a-> t` is a finite labelled transition relation;
- `O:S->Y` is the current-state observation;
- `M` is either set semantics or multiplicity-sensitive Counter semantics;
- `D` is a finite maximum depth or all finite depths.

For set semantics, duplicate transitions to the same quotient class are invisible. For Counter semantics, their multiplicity is retained.

## Definition 1.1 - Depth-zero equivalence

$$s\equiv_0t \iff O(s)=O(t).$$

## Definition 1.2 - Successor profile

Given a partition `P` of `S`, let `[x]_P` denote the block containing `x`. For action `a`, define

$$\mathrm{Succ}^{\mathrm{set}}_P(s,a)=\{[t]_P:s\xrightarrow{a}t\},$$

and

$$\mathrm{Succ}^{\mathrm{cnt}}_P(s,a)=\multiset\{[t]_P:s\xrightarrow{a}t\}.$$

## Definition 1.3 - One refinement step

For `n>=0`,

$$s\equiv_{n+1}t$$

iff `O(s)=O(t)` and for every `a in A`, the declared set or Counter successor profiles of `s` and `t` agree modulo `equiv_n`.

# 2. Stabilization

## Theorem 2.1 - Monotone refinement

For every `n`,

$$\equiv_{n+1}\subseteq\equiv_n.$$

### Proof

The definition of `equiv_(n+1)` retains equality of current observation and adds successor-profile constraints. It can split an `equiv_n` block but cannot merge two blocks already separated. QED.

## Theorem 2.2 - Finite stabilization

If `S` is finite, the sequence stabilizes after at most

$$|S|-|S/\equiv_0|$$

strict refinement steps.

### Proof

Every strict step increases the number of equivalence classes by at least one. The initial partition has `|S/equiv_0|` classes and no partition has more than `|S|`. QED.

Let `equiv_*` denote the stable relation.

---

# 3. Coarsest observer-respecting congruence

## Definition 3.1 - Observer-respecting stable equivalence

An equivalence relation `R` on `S` is observer-respecting if `s R t` implies `O(s)=O(t)`. It is transition-stable if for every action, the declared successor profiles agree after successors are replaced by their `R` classes. With set-valued successors this is the usual block formulation of strong bisimulation. With Counter-valued successors it is the corresponding exact multiplicity-stable congruence.

## Theorem 3.2 - Fixed-point stability

`equiv_*` is an observer-respecting transition-stable equivalence.

### Proof

Stability means the refinement operator leaves the partition unchanged. Therefore every pair in one stable block has equal observation and equal action-labelled successor profiles into stable blocks. QED.

## Theorem 3.3 - Coarsestness

If `R` is any observer-respecting transition-stable equivalence, then

$$R\subseteq\equiv_*.$$

### Proof

Induct on `n`. Observer respect gives `R subseteq equiv_0`. Suppose `R subseteq equiv_n`. If `s R t`, transition stability gives equal successor profiles modulo `R`. Replacing the finer `R` classes by their containing `equiv_n` classes preserves equality, so `s equiv_(n+1) t`. Thus `R subseteq equiv_n` for all `n`, hence `R subseteq equiv_*`. QED.

## Corollary 3.4 - Uniqueness

`equiv_*` is the unique coarsest observer-respecting transition-stable equivalence under the declared successor semantics. In the set-valued case this is the coarsest strong bisimulation; in the Counter case it is the coarsest multiplicity-stable congruence.

---

# 4. Finite observation trees

## Definition 4.1 - Observation tree

Let `Tree_0(s)=O(s)`. Recursively, `Tree_(n+1)(s)` consists of `O(s)` together with, for every action `a`, the set or Counter of `Tree_n` values of all `a` successors.

## Theorem 4.2 - Refinement/tree equivalence

For all `n`,

$$s\equiv_nt \iff \mathrm{Tree}_n(s)=\mathrm{Tree}_n(t).$$

### Proof

Induct on `n`. The base case is Definition 1.1. The inductive step is exactly the refinement definition after replacing successor states by their depth-`n` tree classes. QED.

## Theorem 4.3 - Bounded-depth observational minimality

For every finite depth `d`, the partition `P_d` is exactly equality of depth-`d` action-labelled observation trees. Hence it is the coarsest quotient preserving that bounded observer question. It need not be stable for additional future transitions.

## Theorem 4.4 - Full abstraction for all finite trees

For finite `S`,

$$s\equiv_*t \iff \mathrm{Tree}_n(s)=\mathrm{Tree}_n(t)\quad\forall n<\infty.$$

### Proof

After stabilization at depth `N`, `equiv_n=equiv_*` for all `n>=N`. Apply Theorem 4.2. QED.

## Corollary 4.5 - Finite separator extraction

If `s` and `t` are not `equiv_*` equivalent, there is a finite action-labelled observation tree distinguishing them. The least refinement round at which they split bounds the separator depth.

# Part I - The question made precise

## 1. Sufficiency is not minimality

The closed finite algebra was designed to support exact substitution. If a microscopic composite `X` is replaced by its complete boundary relation `T_X`, every later legal composition produces the same full relation and the same tied-max selection, modulo anonymous-interface isomorphism. This is a soundness or sufficiency theorem:

$$q(x)=q(y) \Longrightarrow x\equiv_{\mathrm{ctx}}y.$$

Here `q` is the canonical boundary map and contextual equivalence means that no admitted finite context distinguishes the two objects.

This implication is the one needed for safe black-box replacement. It says the boundary never hides information that the frozen compositor can later require.

Minimality asks for the converse:

$$x\equiv_{\mathrm{ctx}}y \Longrightarrow q(x)=q(y).$$

If both directions hold, the boundary is fully abstract relative to the chosen observation and context language. But the phrase “chosen observation” cannot be omitted. A context that is allowed to read the complete exact boundary distinguishes every different exact record immediately. A context that asks only “Can this endpoint connect?” can collapse distinctions that exact successor identity needs.

### Plain-language version

A passport contains more information than a ticket inspector needs. It may still be the right exact document for international travel. Asking whether the passport is “minimal” makes no sense until we say which official is looking and what decision that official must make.

# 1. Observer contracts

Let

$$\mathfrak O=(S,A,\to,O,M,D)$$

be an observer contract, where:

- `S` is a finite set of states;
- `A` is a finite action alphabet;
- `s -a-> t` is a finite labelled transition relation;
- `O:S->Y` is the current-state observation;
- `M` is either set semantics or multiplicity-sensitive Counter semantics;
- `D` is a finite maximum depth or all finite depths.

For set semantics, duplicate transitions to the same quotient class are invisible. For Counter semantics, their multiplicity is retained.

## Definition 1.1 - Depth-zero equivalence

$$s\equiv_0t \iff O(s)=O(t).$$

## Definition 1.2 - Successor profile

Given a partition `P` of `S`, let `[x]_P` denote the block containing `x`. For action `a`, define

$$\mathrm{Succ}^{\mathrm{set}}_P(s,a)=\{[t]_P:s\xrightarrow{a}t\},$$

and

$$\mathrm{Succ}^{\mathrm{cnt}}_P(s,a)=\multiset\{[t]_P:s\xrightarrow{a}t\}.$$

## Definition 1.3 - One refinement step

For `n>=0`,

$$s\equiv_{n+1}t$$

iff `O(s)=O(t)` and for every `a in A`, the declared set or Counter successor profiles of `s` and `t` agree modulo `equiv_n`.

# 2. Stabilization

## Theorem 2.1 - Monotone refinement

For every `n`,

$$\equiv_{n+1}\subseteq\equiv_n.$$

### Proof

The definition of `equiv_(n+1)` retains equality of current observation and adds successor-profile constraints. It can split an `equiv_n` block but cannot merge two blocks already separated. QED.

## Theorem 2.2 - Finite stabilization

If `S` is finite, the sequence stabilizes after at most

$$|S|-|S/\equiv_0|$$

strict refinement steps.

### Proof

Every strict step increases the number of equivalence classes by at least one. The initial partition has `|S/equiv_0|` classes and no partition has more than `|S|`. QED.

Let `equiv_*` denote the stable relation.

---

# 3. Coarsest observer-respecting congruence

## Definition 3.1 - Observer-respecting strong bisimulation

An equivalence relation `R` on `S` is observer-respecting if `s R t` implies `O(s)=O(t)`. It is transition-stable if for every action, the declared successor profiles agree after successors are replaced by their `R` classes.

## Theorem 3.2 - Fixed-point stability

`equiv_*` is an observer-respecting transition-stable equivalence.

### Proof

Stability means the refinement operator leaves the partition unchanged. Therefore every pair in one stable block has equal observation and equal action-labelled successor profiles into stable blocks. QED.

## Theorem 3.3 - Coarsestness

If `R` is any observer-respecting transition-stable equivalence, then

$$R\subseteq\equiv_*.$$

### Proof

Induct on `n`. Observer respect gives `R subseteq equiv_0`. Suppose `R subseteq equiv_n`. If `s R t`, transition stability gives equal successor profiles modulo `R`. Replacing the finer `R` classes by their containing `equiv_n` classes preserves equality, so `s equiv_(n+1) t`. Thus `R subseteq equiv_n` for all `n`, hence `R subseteq equiv_*`. QED.

## Corollary 3.4 - Uniqueness

`equiv_*` is the unique coarsest observer-respecting strong bisimulation.

# 4. Finite observation trees

## Definition 4.1 - Observation tree

Let `Tree_0(s)=O(s)`. Recursively, `Tree_(n+1)(s)` consists of `O(s)` together with, for every action `a`, the set or Counter of `Tree_n` values of all `a` successors.

## Theorem 4.2 - Refinement/tree equivalence

For all `n`,

$$s\equiv_nt \iff \mathrm{Tree}_n(s)=\mathrm{Tree}_n(t).$$

### Proof

Induct on `n`. The base case is Definition 1.1. The inductive step is exactly the refinement definition after replacing successor states by their depth-`n` tree classes. QED.

## Theorem 4.3 - Full abstraction for all finite trees

For finite `S`,

$$s\equiv_*t \iff \mathrm{Tree}_n(s)=\mathrm{Tree}_n(t)\quad\forall n<\infty.$$

### Proof

After stabilization at depth `N`, `equiv_n=equiv_*` for all `n>=N`. Apply Theorem 4.2. QED.

## Corollary 4.4 - Finite separator extraction

If `s` and `t` are not `equiv_*` equivalent, there is a finite action-labelled observation tree distinguishing them. The least refinement round at which they split bounds the separator depth.
